units.text: INT. BARBARA - CONTINUOUS
In West Ham. At the sign of the cross. Ask anybody in Canning Town. Where are your works?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: In Perivale St Andrews. At the sign of the sword. Ask anybody in Europe.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Hadn't I better play something?
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Yes. Give us Onward, Christian Soldiers.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Well, that's rather a strong order to begin with, don't you know. Suppose I sing Thou'rt passing hence, my brother. It's much the same tune.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: It's too melancholy. You get saved, Cholly; and you'll pass hence, my brother, without making such a fuss about it.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Really, Barbara, you go on as if religion were a pleasant subject. Do have some sense of propriety.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: I do not find it an unpleasant subject, my dear. It is the only one that capable people really care for.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: LADY BRITOMART [looking at her watch] Well, if you are determined to have it, I insist on having it in a proper and respectable way.
Charles: ring for prayers. [General amazement.
Stephen rises in dismay].
LOMAX [rising] Oh I say!
UNDERSHAFT [rising] I am afraid I must be going.
You cannot go now, Andrew: it would be most improper. Sit down. What will the servants think?
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: My dear: I have conscientious scruples. May I suggest a compromise? If Barbara will conduct a little service in the drawingroom, with Mr Lomax as organist, I will attend it willingly. I will even take part, if a trombone can be procured.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Don't mock, Andrew.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: UNDERSHAFT [shocked--to Barbara] You don't think I am mocking, my love, I hope.
No, of course not; and it wouldn't matter if you were: half the Army came to their first meeting for a lark.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Rising.
Come along. Come, Dolly. Come, Cholly.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: She goes out with Undershaft, who opens the door for her.
Cusins rises.
I will not be disobeyed by everybody. Adolphus: sit down. Charles: you may go. You are not fit for prayers: you cannot keep your countenance.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: Oh I say!
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: He goes out.
LADY BRITOMART [continuing] But you, Adolphus, can behave yourself if you choose to.
I insist on your staying.
My dear Lady Brit: there are things in the family prayer book that I couldn't bear to hear you say.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: What things, pray?
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: Well, you would have to say before all the servants that we have done things we ought not to have done, and left undone things we ought to have done, and that there is no health in us. I cannot bear to hear you doing yourself such an unjustice, and Barbara such an injustice. As for myself, I flatly deny it: I have done my best. I shouldn't dare to marry Barbara--I couldn't look you in the face--if it were true. So I must go to the drawingroom.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: LADY BRITOMART [offended] Well, go. [He starts for the door].
And remember this, Adolphus [he turns to listen]: I have a very strong suspicion that you went to the Salvation Army to worship Barbara and nothing else.
And I quite appreciate the very clever way in which you systematically humbug me.
I have found you out.
Take care Barbara doesn't.
That's all.
CUSINS [with unruffled sweetness] Don't tell on me. [He goes out].
Sarah: if you want to go, go. Anything's better than to sit there as if you wished you were a thousand miles away.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: SARAH [languidly] Very well, mamma. [She goes].
Lady Britomart, with a sudden flounce, gives way to a little gust of tears.
STEPHEN [going to her] Mother: what's the matter?
LADY BRITOMART [swishing away her tears with her handkerchief] Nothing.
Foolishness.
You can go with him, too, if you like, and leave me with the servants.
Oh, you mustn't think that, mother. I--I don't like him.
units.name: STEPHEN

units.text: The others do. That is the injustice of a woman's lot. A woman has to bring up her children; and that means to restrain them, to deny them things they want, to set them tasks, to punish them when they do wrong, to do all the unpleasant things. And then the father, who has nothing to do but pet them and spoil them, comes in when all her work is done and steals their affection from her.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: He has not stolen our affection from you. It is only curiosity.
units.name: STEPHEN

units.text: LADY BRITOMART [violently] I won't be consoled, Stephen.
There is nothing the matter with me. [She rises and goes towards the door].
Where are you going, mother?
units.name: STEPHEN

units.text: To the drawingroom, of course.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: She goes out.
Onward, Christian Soldiers, on the concertina, with tambourine accompaniment, is heard when the door opens.
Are you coming, Stephen?
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: No. Certainly not.
units.name: STEPHEN

units.text: She goes.
He sits down on the settee, with compressed lips and an expression of strong dislike.
The yard of the West Ham shelter of the Salvation Army is a cold place on a January morning.
The building itself, an old warehouse, is newly whitewashed.

Its gabled end projects into the yard in the middle, with a door on the ground floor, and another in the loft above it without any balcony or ladder, but with a pulley rigged over it for hoisting sacks.

Those who come from this central gable end into the yard have the gateway leading to the street on their left, with a stone horse-trough just beyond it, and, on the right, a penthouse shielding a table from the weather.

There are forms at the table; and on them are seated a man and a woman, both much down on their luck, finishing a meal of bread [one thick slice each, with margarine and golden syrup] and diluted milk.
The man, a workman out of employment, is young, agile, a talker, a poser, sharp enough to be capable of anything in reason except honesty or altruistic considerations of any kind.
The woman is a commonplace old bundle of poverty and hard-worn humanity.
She looks sixty and probably is forty-five.

If they were rich people, gloved and muffed and well wrapped up in furs and overcoats, they would be numbed and miserable; for it is a grindingly cold, raw, January day; and a glance at the background of grimy warehouses and leaden sky visible over the whitewashed walls of the yard would drive any idle rich person straight to the Mediterranean.

But these two, being no more troubled with visions of the Mediterranean than of the moon, and being compelled to keep more of their clothes in the pawnshop, and less on their persons, in winter than in summer, are not depressed by the cold: rather are they stung into vivacity, to which their meal has just now given an almost jolly turn.
The man takes a pull at his mug, and then gets up and moves about the yard with his hands deep in his pockets, occasionally breaking into a stepdance.
